name: ps
purpose: Process Status — list currently running processes.
explanation: Plain 'ps' shows only processes associated with the current terminal session. 'ps aux' shows ALL processes running system-wide, including columns for USER (owner), PID (Process ID), %CPU, %MEM, and COMMAND.

parameters.description: Shows all system-wide processes with USER, PID, %CPU, %MEM, and COMMAND columns.

whenToUse: To inspect running processes and find a Process ID (PID) for monitoring or termination.
commonMistakes: Running plain 'ps' and wondering why background/GUI apps like Chrome are not listed.
